items.headline: BYD confirms humanoid-robot development, floats dealer-network distribution
items.diff_narrative: No antecedent in yesterday's brief, whose embodied-AI / hardware coverage centered on Nvidia's product surface and the chip-stock roster. Today introduces a distinct entrant: BYD publicly confirmed for the first time (Stella Li, June 3 interview; reinforced by Li Ke on June 4) that it is developing humanoid robots, intends to build an open robot platform that can host both in-house and partner products, and could one day sell them through its existing auto dealer network. Chinese reporting adds the program has run since 2022 under BYD's electronic-integration unit, is codenamed "Yao-Shun-Yu," and already has factory-floor prototypes under test. The angle is that the humanoid cohort now extends from robotics specialists and Tesla to a vertically integrated automaker that owns the motor, cell, sensor, and silicon supply chains plus a consumer channel.

items.headline: Broadcom's softer AI-chip guidance triggers a multi-day semiconductor sell-off
items.diff_narrative: This is the same AI-accelerator-equity thread as yesterday's China Renaissance Nvidia initiation, but the polarity flips. Yesterday's item was a single bullish catalyst — a new desk opening Nvidia at Buy with a $319 target, read as reinforcing the soft-landing demand view. Today the same complex sells off: Broadcom's fiscal Q2 (after the close June 3) beat on revenue and EPS but guided Q3 AI semiconductor revenue to about $16B against a roughly $17.2B consensus and declined to raise its full-year 2026 AI forecast, read as a sell-the-news miss; the stock fell about 15% on June 4. The drawdown spread across the group — Micron off about 7% on June 4, then a second down day on June 5 (Micron about 3.3%, Intel about 2.8%, AMD about 2.8%, Nvidia about 1.4%) compounded by a memory-pricing crisis and a forecast record drop in smartphone volumes. The center of gravity moves from one analyst's upgrade to a sector-wide repricing, and the read inverts from soft-landing confidence to AI-hardware equities being priced for continuous beat-and-raise, so a merely-solid quarter now drags correlated names down.

items.headline: DeployBench benchmarks LLM agents on research-artifact deployment; best model stalls at 51%
items.diff_narrative: Absent from yesterday's brief, which had no agent-evaluation or benchmark item. Today adds a new arxiv benchmark, DeployBench (arxiv 2606.05238, submitted June 3): a 51-task suite across AI/ML, computer systems, and scientific computing that measures whether an agent can take a paper's released code and stand up a working environment from scratch (multi-language toolchains, system-level dependencies beyond containers, legacy compatibility). Four state-of-the-art LLMs run inside the OpenHands harness score pass rates of just 7.8% to 51.0%. The instructive finding is the dominant "completion-judgment problem" error mode — agent-terminated self-stops where the agent declares success against a weaker target than the task requires — pointing at verification, not raw capability, as the binding constraint on autonomous deployment.

items.headline: AI events to plan around: WWDC opens Monday across the three-track calendar
items.diff_narrative: The same three-track events roundup (mainstream / AI-security / AI-chip) carried forward from yesterday, anchored this run on a fresh date-reached catalyst: Apple WWDC26 opens this coming Monday June 8 (keynote 10:00 AM PT, through June 12), with coverage now expecting a chatbot-style Siri overhaul with on-screen awareness plus the iOS/macOS 27 generation. Carried with sharper detail: the Confidential Computing Summit (June 23-24) now names an NVIDIA confidential-computing attestation session and hardware-verified attestation; the Databricks Data + AI Summit (June 15-18) gains scale figures (30,000-plus in person, 800-plus sessions) and a recorded Satya Nadella fireside alongside Greg Brockman; the AI Engineer World's Fair is detailed as 29 tracks including multiple agentic tracks. Dropped: The AI Summit London (June 10-11), carried yesterday, is not in today's bullet. Shifted: AMD's Advancing AI event softens from firm July 22-23 dates to July (Moscone SF) and gains MI400 / MI455X availability framing. Hot Chips (Stanford Aug 23-25), AI Infra Summit (Santa Clara Sept 15-17), Black Hat AI Summit, DEF CON 34 AI Village, OWASP Global AppSec USA, GitHub Universe, AWS re:Invent, and the Zenity expansion all persist.
